title: Psilocybin, Senate Race Highlight Harvard Year
author: Efrem Sigel
summary: The Harvard Crimson's July 1963 year-in-review covers Richard Alpert's May dismissal for giving psilocybin to an undergraduate and Timothy Leary's suspension. The article traces the dispute from March 1962 through the November 1962 warning by Dean Monro and Dr. Farnsworth.
excerpt: President Pusey announced on May 27 that the Corporation had terminated the appointment of Richard Alpert as assistant professor of Clinical Psychology and of Education for giving hallucinogenic drugs to an undergraduate in violation of an agreement with the University. The dismissal, the first in Pusey's ten years at Harvard, climaxed more than a year of off-and-on controversey [sic] over the work of Alpert and an associate, Timothy Leary, Lecturer on Clinical Psychology, with psilocybin.
citation: Efrem Sigel, "Psilocybin, Senate Race Highlight Harvard Year," The Harvard Crimson, July 9, 1963.
